sketch.title: Funnel into diverge
sketch.caption: The piece funnels from a broad problem (how do neurons process information?) down to one tool (partial information decomposition), then fans that tool out into several empirical findings before closing with limits and future extensions — a funnel into a diverge.

scenes.title: From a broad question to a tool to its findings

items.text: How do brains process information?
Old limits: too little data, no good tools
Mutual information & transfer entropy track flow
Flow alone can't show how inputs combine
Joint information splits into redundant, unique, synergistic parts
General case needs a lattice and a redundancy measure
Rich-club neurons do most of the synergistic computing
Synergy rises with feedforward & recurrent links
Synergy peaks at moderate input similarity
In behaving monkeys, redundancy rises during movement
Practical limits: data type, sample size, software choice
Future: time-resolved local PID, multi-target decomposition
Neurons compute on patterns, not just totals

scenes.caption: The argument narrows from the general problem of neural information processing down to the PID framework, then spreads out into the empirical discoveries PID has produced, before considering limits and extensions.

scenes.title: Building the decomposition

items.text: Joint info ≠ sum of individual inputs' info
Whole > parts: synergy (joint pattern matters)
Whole < parts: redundancy (repeated info)
Two-parent case: four atoms, three equations
System is underdetermined without a redundancy function
General case: sources form a lattice of atoms
Atoms computed recursively via Mobius inversion
No single agreed redundancy measure exists

scenes.caption: PID starts from a simple imbalance (the whole input isn't the sum of its parts), builds intuition with two inputs, then generalizes via a lattice that needs a chosen redundancy measure.

scenes.title: What PID found in real circuits

items.text: Thousands of neuron triads decomposed via PID
Rich-club triads hold ~88% of network synergy
More recurrent links, more synergy; feedback adds little
Synergy peaks at moderate source correlation, then falls
Caveat: bivariate estimates and cultured tissue, not live behavior
Same method applied to macaques doing a motor task
Redundancy rises sharply during movement execution
Synergy structure tracks behavior, not just anatomy

scenes.caption: Three independent empirical threads from cultured cortical networks converge on where and why synergy occurs, then a shift to behaving animals shows the same framework adapting to task demands.

plates.title: The Funnel and the Fan
plates.prompt: An illuminated manuscript page on aged parchment, sepia ink with gold leaf accents, one continuous vertical composition read top to bottom, all scenes set in small roundels linked by painted vine-tendrils that branch and rejoin like a river delta. At the top, THE GRAND CHALLENGE: a scholar gazing at a glowing brain-shaped pathway-map with rays entering from drawn eyes and ears. Below it, FLOW WITHOUT INTERACTION: two unmixed ribbons of light passing through a stone channel. Next, TWO CIRCLES OVERLAPPING: a red and a blue circle overlapping within a larger oval, the overlap cross-hatched. Below that, THE LATTICE OF ATOMS: a tiered trellis of small coloured jewel-nodes on threads. From the lattice the vine-path splits into three roundels set side by side across the page's width: THE RICH CLUB'S SHARE (a bright knot of nodes glowing within a faint wider web), THE LOOPED TRIAD (three nodes with a bright looping double arrow between two of them), and THE PEAK BEFORE THE FALL (a hill with a flag planted short of its summit). These three tendrils braid back together into one roundel below: THREE MACAQUES AT WORK, three macaques with fine recording leads at a hand-task table. From there the path splits again into two roundels side by side: THE GRID OF ZEROS AND ONES (a scholar dwarfed by an endless ledger of painted 0s and 1s) and THE NEURONAL AVALANCHE (a cascade of sparks in shaded bands tumbling down a slope). These two tendrils rejoin at the bottom in one final roundel: READING THE PATTERN, NOT THE SUM, a gatekeeper-figure studying the arrangement of arrows at a neuron's threshold rather than counting them. Palette restricted to browns, dull reds, blues, and gold leaf highlights on cream parchment; linework fine and slightly irregular as if drawn by hand with a reed pen. Each roundel has its title lettered in small capitals on a plain ribbon directly beneath it, and nothing else on the page carries any lettering at all — no headings, no scrolls, no signatures, no other words anywhere. Leave generous bare parchment between roundels; do not crowd the margins with ornament.

vignettes.quote: A grand challenge of modern neuroscience is to discover how brains “process information”.

vignettes.title: THE GRAND CHALLENGE

vignettes.quote: represented by the red circle for I(X1;Y) and the blue circle for I(X2;Y)

vignettes.title: TWO CIRCLES OVERLAPPING

vignettes.quote: Lattice vertices are partial information atoms, i.e., the unique modes of information-sharing that comprise the overall joint mutual information.
vignettes.depicts: A tiered trellis of small jewel-like nodes strung on threads in ascending rows, each jewel a distinct colour, like a genealogical vine of gems.
vignettes.title: THE LATTICE OF ATOMS

vignettes.quote: 20% of the neurons account for 70% of the information propagation in organotypic cortical cultures

vignettes.title: THE RICH CLUB'S SHARE

vignettes.quote: triads with two recurrent connections and no feedback connections had 50% more synergy

vignettes.title: THE LOOPED TRIAD

vignettes.quote: The peak in synergy occurred when the mutual information was about 7% of the maximal value, regardless of the timescale.
vignettes.depicts: A painted hill with a small flag planted partway up its slope rather than at the summit, marking a peak that is not the highest point.
vignettes.title: THE PEAK BEFORE THE FALL

vignettes.quote: For a system of binary elements such as spiking neurons, there are 2 k possible combinations of 0s and 1s.
vignettes.depicts: A scholar stands before an endless ledger-grid of tiny painted zeros and ones stretching past the page's edge, quill raised, overwhelmed by its size.
vignettes.title: THE GRID OF ZEROS AND ONES

vignettes.quote: finding that neuronal avalanches (a common signature of complex, critical dynamics in the nervous system) have distinct “computational profiles”
vignettes.depicts: A cascade of sparks tumbles down a slope in bands of changing colour, each band of the avalanche shaded differently from the one above it.
vignettes.title: THE NEURONAL AVALANCHE

vignettes.quote: neurons do not appear to blindly sum the number of inputs and fire in response to the total
vignettes.depicts: A single gatekeeper-figure at a neuron's threshold studies the arrangement of several arriving arrows rather than merely stacking and counting them.
vignettes.title: READING THE PATTERN, NOT THE SUM

plates.title: Inside the Decomposition
plates.prompt: An illuminated manuscript page on aged parchment, sepia ink and gold leaf, in the same hand and palette as a prior plate in this set. The whole page is bordered by a repeating trellis-of-jewels motif — the same lattice pattern that appears partway down the page — so the border itself signals this plate is the inside of the lattice portion of a larger map. Inside the border, roundels run top to bottom linked by vine-tendrils. At top, WHOLE VERSUS PARTS: an old balance scale with one large stone on one pan and several smaller stones on the other, unlevel. The tendril forks into two roundels side by side: THE WEAVING NEURON (a weaver-figure braiding several coloured threads into one new pattern at a target cell) and COUNTED TWICE (a scribe tallying one duplicated coin twice from two parent-nodes). These rejoin into TWO PARENTS, ONE TARGET: two tree-like cells each sending a thread down to one small target cell. Below that, THREE KNOWN, FOUR UNKNOWN: a scribe with three open coffers and four locked chests on his table, puzzling over the imbalance. Next, ATOMS ON THE TRELLIS: the tiered trellis of jewel-nodes on threads, matching the page's own border pattern, marking this as the heart of the lattice. Below it, THE RECURSIVE STAIRCASE: a hooded figure descending a spiral stair, setting a jewel on each step whose light feeds the step above. At the bottom, A DOZEN RIVAL MEASURES: twelve robed figures in a loose circle, each holding a different measuring instrument, disagreeing. Palette of browns, dull reds, blues and gold leaf on cream parchment, fine irregular reed-pen linework. Each roundel has its title lettered in small capitals beneath it on a plain ribbon, and nothing else on the page is lettered anywhere — no headings, no scrolls, no signatures. Leave open parchment between roundels; do not crowd the border ornament inward over the scenes.

plates.title: Inside the Empirical Findings
plates.prompt: An illuminated manuscript page on aged parchment, sepia ink and gold leaf, in the same hand and palette as the other plates in this set. Roundels run top to bottom linked by vine-tendrils in painted ink. At the top, THE 512-CHANNEL ARRAY: a thin disc of cortical tissue resting on a wide grid of electrode points beneath a brass microscope stand. The tendril forks into three roundels set side by side across the page: RICH CLUB'S LION'S SHARE (a small bright knot of nodes outshining a large faint web around it), THE DOUBLE LOOP (three nodes with a bright looping double arrow between two of them, beside a fainter plain triad), and THE PEAK BEFORE THE FALL (a hill with a flag short of its summit and the slope falling away beyond it) — the same bright-cluster, looped-triad, and flagged-hill motifs as appear earlier in this set, so the reader recognises each as the same finding. These three tendrils rejoin into one roundel: CULTURE VERSUS LIVING BRAIN, a glass dish with cultured tissue set apart from a distant living animal, a faint dotted path bridging the gap between them. Below that, THE SERIAL CONDITIONING CHAIN: a scribe tracing a chain of linked beads point by point across a table. Next, THE REACH AND GRASP: one of three seated macaques (recalling the macaques of the earlier plate) reaching out to grasp an object, many duplicate glowing threads streaming from head to hand. At the bottom, SYNERGY FOLLOWS BEHAVIOR: a macaque figure whose pattern of light across marked brain regions visibly differs between two postures. Palette restricted to browns, dull reds, blues and gold leaf on cream parchment, fine irregular reed-pen linework, consistent with the rest of the set. Each roundel has its title lettered in small capitals on a plain ribbon beneath it, and nothing else on the page carries any lettering whatsoever — no headings, no scrolls, no signatures, no inscriptions. Leave open bare parchment between roundels rather than crowding the page with border ornament.

questions.referenceAnswer: A lack of sufficient recorded data, since studying how neurons jointly share information requires large amounts of data to accurately infer patterns across many neurons; this was eased by new high-density recording technologies.

questions.question: What was the second limitation that remained even after large amounts of recorded data became available?

questions.question: What framework did the researchers turn to in order to directly examine how a target neuron's information is produced from the interaction of its input sources?
questions.premise: Transfer entropy can't show how multiple inputs interact, since it only tracks each source separately.
questions.referenceAnswer: Partial information decomposition (PID), which splits the information that multiple sources jointly provide about a target into redundant, unique, and synergistic parts.

evidence.quote: This parsing is accomplished using the partial information decomposition (PID) framework [20].

questions.question: Why does extending PID from two parent neurons to three or more require more complex mathematical machinery, such as a lattice structure?

evidence.quote: Unfortunately, in the case of three or more parents, the resulting system of equations is not as constrained as in the two-element case, as the number of distinct partial information atoms grows much faster than the number of known mutual information terms. questions.question: What systematic bias affects naive ('plug-in') estimates of entropy and mutual information from limited data?

questions.question: According to the summary, what does the existence of synergy suggest about how neurons respond to their inputs, compared with a simple threshold or summing model?

evidence.quote: The existence of synergy in empirical data shows us that neurons do not appear to blindly sum the number of inputs and fire in response to the total (as would be expected from a basic threshold model or complex contagion model), but instead they are also sensitive to the particular patterns of incoming stimuli.

In this case, the system exhibits synergistic dynamics, and the target neuron can be thought of as performing a kind of integrating "computation" on all of its inputs considered jointly
occurrences.reasoning: States directly that a surplus of joint over individual information is interpreted as the target neuron computing, not just passing signals along.

occurrences.quote: Information transfer captures the overall "flow" of information through the system; however, it is limited in its ability to reveal how different streams of information "interact" and how neurons produce novel or modified information from multiple sources
occurrences.reasoning: Motivates the whole move to decomposition by contrasting mere flow with interaction/production of new information, i.e. computation.

occurrences.quote: The existence of synergy in empirical data shows us that neurons do not appear to blindly sum the number of inputs and fire in response to the total (as would be expected from a basic threshold model or complex contagion model), but instead they are also sensitive to the particular patterns of incoming stimuli.
occurrences.reasoning: Concludes the whole review by cashing out synergy as evidence of pattern-sensitive computation, confirming this is the idea the reader was meant to take away.

ideas.name: Joint information splits into four exhaustive parts
ideas.statement: The total information two sources carry about a target can be broken, without overlap or leftover, into information redundantly available from either source, information unique to each source, and information only available from their joint pattern (synergy).

occurrences.quote: Red(X₁, X₂;Y) is the information about Y that could be learned by observing X₁ or X₂, Unq(Xᵢ;Y) is the information about Y that could only be learned by observing Xᵢ, and Syn(X₁, X₂;Y) is the information about Y that can only be learned by observing the joint states of X₁ and X₂ together.
occurrences.reasoning: Defines the four named components that together are claimed to exhaust the joint information.

occurrences.quote: These independent sources can carry redundant information, represented by the overlapping striped section labeled Red(X1, X2;Y). The non-redundant information each source neuron accounts for is the unique information Unq(X1;Y) and Unq(X2;Y).
occurrences.reasoning: Illustrates the same four-way split visually, reinforcing that these are meant as non-overlapping pieces of one total.

ideas.name: Redundancy measure needed to resolve PID's underdetermination
ideas.statement: Because classical information theory gives only three known quantities (the joint and two marginal mutual informations) but four unknown pieces to solve for, a decomposition is impossible until one separately defines what counts as redundant information; once that choice is made, the rest follow automatically.

occurrences.quote: The result is an underdetermined system of linear equations, with three known values (the mutual information terms) and four unknown values (the partial information terms). If any of the unknown terms can be defined, then the other three emerge "for free".
occurrences.reasoning: States explicitly that the decomposition only becomes solvable once a redundancy (or other) term is independently defined.

occurrences.quote: given a suitable measure of redundancy (which we will refer to as I∩(·)), it is possible to decompose the total joint mutual information into a finite set of unique, partial information atoms based on how all the elements of S share information about Y.
occurrences.reasoning: Generalizes the same dependency on a chosen redundancy function to the full multi-source lattice case.

occurrences.quote: Applying PID analyses to real data requires some notion of redundant information (I∩(·)) to be operationalized. To date, no single universally accepted measure has been proposed.
occurrences.reasoning: Confirms that every practical application hinges on picking among competing redundancy definitions rather than a single agreed solution.

ideas.name: Rich clubs concentrate synergistic computation
ideas.statement: The densely interconnected core of best-connected neurons in a circuit (the rich club) carries a disproportionate share of both information flow and the higher-order, synergistic computation, well beyond what its size would predict.

occurrences.quote: Rich clubs, in the context of the effective networks built from cortical circuit spiking recordings, are comprised of the neurons that propagate the most information (i.e., sending and receiving). By definition, rich clubs are disproportionately dense in information propagation: 20% of the neurons account for 70% of the information propagation in organotypic cortical cultures
occurrences.reasoning: Establishes that the rich club is already known to dominate raw information flow, setting up the synergy finding.

occurrences.quote: Unambiguously, rich club triads processed more information than triads outside rich clubs. Numerically, the triads inside the rich clubs had 2.7 times the amount of synergy as the triads not in the rich club
occurrences.reasoning: States the core empirical finding that synergy, not just flow, is concentrated in the rich club.

ideas.name: Recurrent wiring boosts synergy more than feedback does
ideas.statement: Among the three connection types in a two-source, one-target unit, more connections between the two source neurons (recurrence) reliably raise synergy, feedback from the target back to the sources tends to slightly lower it, and the forward connections remain the strongest predictor overall.

occurrences.quote: Feedback connections are those from the target back to the source neurons. There may be zero, one, or two of these in a computational triad. Recurrent connections are connections between the source neurons.
occurrences.reasoning: Defines the three connection categories whose differing effects on synergy the finding depends on.

occurrences.quote: Using PID, we found that triads with more recurrent connections also had greater synergy [4]. Feedback connections were less predictive of synergy but tended to correlate with reduced synergy.
occurrences.reasoning: States the comparative empirical result directly.

ideas.statement: As the two input neurons' activity becomes more similar, the synergy they jointly provide about the target rises only up to a point (around 7% of the maximum possible shared information), after which redundancy takes over and synergy falls, a pattern that holds across a wide range of timescales.

occurrences.quote: The greater the mutual information between source neurons at the synaptic timescale, the greater the synergy [3]. More information processing occurs where similar information streams converge
occurrences.reasoning: Shows the rising portion of the relationship at short timescales.

occurrences.quote: Interestingly, synergy only increased up to a point. The peak in synergy occurred when the mutual information was about 7% of the maximal value, regardless of the timescale. Past this level, the synergy began to decrease
occurrences.reasoning: States the turning point and its generality across timescales, the crux of the idea.

occurrences.quote: This suggests that as the similarity of the converging information grows past some point, it becomes redundant, and the total amount of synergistic output is suppressed.
occurrences.reasoning: Explains the mechanism behind the fall after the peak, completing the non-monotonic picture.

ideas.name: Multi-target decomposition extends PID across time and targets
ideas.statement: The original framework, built for many sources feeding a single target, can be generalized to ask how information is shared, duplicated, or jointly produced across multiple targets at once, including treating a system's own past and future as source and target to study its temporal dynamics.

occurrences.quote: There are, however, a number of later advances that extend the PID framework in potentially fruitful directions.
occurrences.reasoning: Frames multi-target decomposition as part of a family of extensions beyond the classic single-target version covered earlier.

ideas.name: Information decomposition can be localized to single moments
ideas.statement: Rather than only computing redundancy, uniqueness, and synergy as averages over an entire probability distribution, the same decomposition can be applied to one specific observed configuration at a time, yielding a moment-by-moment trace of how information is being shared.

occurrences.quote: the PID framework itself can also be localized to single configurations.
occurrences.reasoning: States the core move of localizing the decomposition away from expected values.

occurrences.quote: The local PID framework allows us to perform the same decomposition, but for every individual possible configuration of specific source and target states.
occurrences.reasoning: Spells out what localizing means in practice: per-configuration decomposition rather than an overall average.

occurrences.quote: For a local PID analysis to be possible, all that is required is that the redundancy function chosen is localizable.
occurrences.reasoning: Gives the condition needed for this time-resolved version of the idea to be usable at all.

quotes.text: Historically, there have been two key limitations hindering the study of information processing by neural circuits. The first was a lack of appropriate data, since the analysis of synergistic dynamics requires large amounts of data to accurately infer the structure of multivariate dependence.
quotes.reason: States the historical obstacle the whole review is framed as overcoming.

quotes.text: Whereas mutual information is a measure of functional connectivity, transfer entropy measures effective connectivity [14]. In other words, transfer entropy provides a measure of information propagation.
quotes.reason: Crisp distinction between the two core measures used before PID is introduced.

quotes.text: Information transfer (discussed above) tells us about how the past of either source Xi informs the future of Y, but to understand “processing”, we are interested in how the interaction between the two source variables’ past influences the target’s future in a way that is not reducible to either source considered individually.
quotes.reason: States why transfer entropy is insufficient and motivates PID.

quotes.text: If the left-hand side of Equation (4) (the “whole”) is greater than the right-hand side (the sum of the “parts”), then there is some information about Y that is disclosed by the joint state of all the neurons that is not disclosed by any individual parent. In this case, the system exhibits synergistic dynamics, and the target neuron can be thought of as performing a kind of integrating “computation” on all of its inputs considered jointly
quotes.reason: Defines synergy, the central concept of the whole review.

quotes.text: Conversely, if the whole is less than the sum of its parts, then there must be redundant information about Y instantiated multiple times over the parent neurons that is “double counted” when summing the marginals.
quotes.reason: Completes the definition pairing redundancy with synergy.

quotes.text: This inequality has been recognized for decades; however, it was not until the seminal work of Williams and Beer [1] that it was recognized how to algebraically decompose the total joint mutual information into the particular contributions of the parts (and higher-order ensembles of parts).
quotes.reason: Credits the founding insight the whole framework builds on.

quotes.text: The result is an underdetermined system of linear equations, with three known values (the mutual information terms) and four unknown values (the partial information terms). If any of the unknown terms can be defined, then the other three emerge “for free”. Unfortunately, classical Shannon information theory provides no unique solution to any of these, and so considerable work has been devoted to developing formal measures of each.
quotes.reason: Explains the core mathematical problem that makes choosing a redundancy function necessary.

quotes.text: To date, no single universally accepted measure has been proposed. All measures have their own trade-offs and drawbacks (such as only being defined for systems of a fixed size, only being amenable to discrete random variables, or requiring arbitrary thresholds).
quotes.reason: Honest statement of an unresolved problem at the heart of PID methodology.

quotes.text: When we performed this analysis, examining 25 separate recordings at timescales varying from 1 ms to 14 ms, we found that synergy was strongly correlated (ρ ≫ 0.57 for all recordings and timescales; see Figure 4A). Interestingly, this analysis revealed that—for these recordings—the amount of synergy observed in a given triad was reliably about a quarter of the transfer entropy for that triad [2]. The implication of this is that feedforward information propagation between source neurons and a target neuron is a reliable predictor of information processing.
quotes.reason: Key empirical finding linking information flow to computation, with a concrete numeric result.

quotes.text: Unambiguously, rich club triads processed more information than triads outside rich clubs. Numerically, the triads inside the rich clubs had 2.7 times the amount of synergy as the triads not in the rich club (Figure 4B).
quotes.reason: Central empirical result tying network hubs to computation.

quotes.text: Despite the fact that that less than 40% of the neurons were in the rich club, the rich club triads accounted for ∼88% of the network-wide synergy.
quotes.reason: Striking numeric payoff showing extreme concentration of computation in rich clubs.

quotes.text: Using PID, we found that triads with more recurrent connections also had greater synergy [4]. Feedback connections were less predictive of synergy but tended to correlate with reduced synergy.
quotes.reason: Summarizes the structural finding about recurrent versus feedback connectivity.

quotes.text: The result was unambiguous. The greater the mutual information between source neurons at the synaptic timescale, the greater the synergy [3]. More information processing occurs where similar information streams converge (Figure 4E, the three leftmost panels for synaptic timescales).
quotes.reason: States a clear, surprising empirical relationship between correlated inputs and computation.

quotes.text: Interestingly, synergy only increased up to a point. The peak in synergy occurred when the mutual information was about 7% of the maximal value, regardless of the timescale. Past this level, the synergy began to decrease (this level is marked by the vertical dotted line in Figure 4E).
quotes.reason: Describes the non-monotonic relationship that is a key nuanced finding of the work.

quotes.text: This suggests that as the similarity of the converging information grows past some point, it becomes redundant, and the total amount of synergistic output is suppressed.
quotes.reason: Explains the mechanism behind the non-monotonic synergy-redundancy tradeoff.

quotes.text: The researchers found that while brain activity was generally synergy-dominated (as opposed to redundancy-dominated), during movement execution (a reach-and-grasp action) the relative abundance of redundant information increased dramatically.
quotes.reason: Key finding from the primate study showing task-dependent shifts in information processing mode.

quotes.text: This increase in relative redundancy was interpreted as a response to the practical requirements of the task: during motor execution, the brain needs to send the “move” signal to distant muscles, and to ensure high-fidelity transmission the brain may duplicate information many times over (minimizing the risk of a single corrupted signal leading to erroneous behavior).
quotes.reason: Offers a compelling functional interpretation of why redundancy rises during movement.

quotes.text: These results show not only that synergistic information dynamics is a feature of ongoing, spontaneous neural activity but also that synergy seems to reflect behaviorally specific patterns of dynamical activity in the cortex.
quotes.reason: Summary conclusion of the primate behavioral study section.

quotes.text: One important caveat to note with respect to PID applied to neural data is that while it provides a powerful framework for recognizing statistical dependencies between neurons, it does not necessarily provide a mechanistic explanation for why particular neurons are synergy-dominated or redundancy-dominated.
quotes.reason: Important methodological caveat limiting overinterpretation of PID results.

quotes.text: The most significant is the explosive growth of the PI lattice. For a system with k parent neurons, the number of distinct PI atoms is given by the kth Dedekind number (minus two) [30]. This sequence of numbers grows appallingly fast: in the case of six parent neurons, there are 7,828,354 distinct PI atoms, the vast majority of which are difficult to interpret.
quotes.reason: Vivid illustration of a core practical limitation of the framework.

quotes.text: Given that single neurons can receive inputs from very large numbers of upstream neurons, a “complete” description of the information dynamics of any individual neuron is completely intractable.
quotes.reason: Blunt statement of the scalability ceiling for the method.

quotes.text: The existence of synergy in empirical data shows us that neurons do not appear to blindly sum the number of inputs and fire in response to the total (as would be expected from a basic threshold model or complex contagion model), but instead they are also sensitive to the particular patterns of incoming stimuli.
quotes.reason: The closing thesis statement summarizing what synergy implies about neural computation.

quotes.text: Furthermore, not only does the existence of statistical synergy add nuance and dimensions to our understanding of the dynamics of individual neurons, we have also shown that the patterns of synergistic information processing are informed by the local environment in which those neurons are embedded (rich club membership, motifs, clustering, etc.), as well as the behavioral state of the oganism under study.
quotes.reason: Final synthesis connecting local network structure and behavior to computation.

entries.name: Partial Information Decomposition
entries.senseHere: A mathematical framework that splits the total information two or more sources carry about a target into separate pieces: information shared redundantly, information unique to each source, and information that only appears when sources are combined. The article uses this breakdown to treat the combined-only piece as evidence that a neuron is actively computing on its inputs rather than just adding them up.

entries.name: Rich Club
entries.senseHere: The subset of neurons in a network that are the most strongly interconnected with each other, more densely than chance would predict. The article's recordings show these neurons carry a hugely disproportionate share of the network's synergistic information processing.

entries.name: Mutual Information
entries.senseHere: A measure of how much knowing one neuron's activity reduces uncertainty about another neuron's activity, treated in the article as an undirected, instantaneous statistical dependency rather than a measure of transfer or flow.

entries.name: Transfer Entropy
entries.senseHere: A directional measure of how much a source neuron's past activity reduces uncertainty about a target neuron's future activity, beyond what the target's own past already predicts. The article uses it to quantify information flow between neurons and to build the effective networks that triads are drawn from.

entries.name: Functional Connectivity
entries.senseHere: A description of plain statistical similarity or correlation between two neurons' activity patterns, without any claim about direction or causal flow, which the article contrasts with the directed notion of effective connectivity.

entries.name: Effective Connectivity
entries.senseHere: A description of directed, flow-like influence from one neuron's activity to another's, as distinguished in the article from mere statistical similarity between neurons.

entries.name: Synergy
entries.senseHere: The portion of information about a target neuron's activity that can only be learned by observing two or more source neurons together, and that disappears if you look at any one source alone. The article treats high synergy as a signature of genuine information processing or computation happening at a neuron.

entries.name: Redundancy
entries.senseHere: The information about a target that could be learned equally well from any one of several source neurons on its own, so that counting it from each source separately would double-count it. The article treats rising redundancy as a sign that converging inputs are becoming too similar to add new joint information.

entries.name: Unique Information
entries.senseHere: The piece of information about a target neuron that only one particular source neuron carries, and that no other source could substitute for.

entries.name: Williams and Beer
entries.background: Researchers whose seminal paper first showed how to algebraically split total joint mutual information into redundant, unique, and synergistic components, founding the partial information decomposition framework used throughout this article.

entries.name: Redundancy Function
entries.senseHere: A chosen formula for quantifying how much information counts as redundantly shared between source neurons, which is needed before the rest of the decomposition can be computed since classical information theory leaves this value undetermined. The article notes several competing versions exist, each with different tradeoffs, with Imin being the original and most commonly used in the neuroscience studies it reviews.

entries.name: Computational Triad
entries.senseHere: The basic unit analyzed in the article's experiments: two source neurons that both connect to a single shared target neuron, small enough that partial information decomposition can be fully computed for it.

entries.name: Partial Information Lattice
entries.senseHere: A structured diagram, introduced by Williams and Beer, that organizes all the distinct redundant/unique/synergistic information pieces for a set of sources and a target so each piece can be calculated without double-counting. The article uses it to extend the two-source redundant/unique/synergy picture to any number of source neurons.

entries.name: Mobius Inversion
entries.senseHere: The recursive calculation used to work out the value of each individual information-sharing piece on the partial information lattice, by subtracting out whatever is already accounted for by simpler combinations of sources lower on the lattice.

entries.name: Organotypic Cortical Culture
entries.senseHere: A thin slice of mouse brain cortex kept alive and growing in nutrient fluid outside the body, which restores much of its natural neural connectivity and lets researchers record from hundreds of real neurons over long periods. The article relies on recordings from these cultures as its primary source of large-scale spiking data for PID analysis.

entries.name: Feedforward, Feedback, and Recurrent Connections
entries.senseHere: Within a three-neuron triad, feedforward links run from the two source neurons to the shared target, feedback links run from the target back to the sources, and recurrent links connect the two source neurons to each other. The article finds synergy rises with feedforward and recurrent connection strength but not with feedback.

entries.name: Dedekind Number
entries.senseHere: A rapidly growing count used to tell how many distinct information-sharing pieces appear on the partial information lattice as the number of source neurons grows, explaining why full decompositions become computationally impossible for more than a handful of sources.

entries.name: O-information
entries.senseHere: A simplified, more scalable measure of overall redundancy versus synergy across a whole group of variables, used as a practical substitute when the full partial information decomposition is too complex to compute.

entries.name: Local PID
entries.senseHere: A version of partial information decomposition applied to single, specific moments of neural activity rather than averaged over all possible states, producing a time-resolved trace of redundancy, uniqueness, and synergy as they change moment to moment.

entries.name: Integrated Information Decomposition
entries.senseHere: An extension of partial information decomposition that handles multiple target variables at once, rather than just one, making it possible to track how redundant, unique, and synergistic information flows from a group of sources at one time to a group of targets at a later time. The article mentions it has been used to study changes in brain information flow during loss of consciousness.
